sentences.text: This petition under Section 166 MV act is filed by the Petitioner seeking compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- for the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.

2. The petitioner has stated that on 05.05.2022, at approximately 5:30 PM, he was riding his motorcycle bearing registration number KA-41-ED- 6565 from Bengaluru towards Pavagada, near the Rajavanthi Forest area, opposite Nursery, Tumkur Road, Rajavanthi, Tumkur.

At that time, a car bearing registration number KA-53-C-0388 (hereinafter referred to as the "offending vehicle") came from behind in a rash and negligent manner and collided with the petitioner's motorcycle.
As a result of the impact, the petitioner fell and sustained grievous injuries.
3. Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to A.R. Hospital, Hindupura, where he was admitted as an inpatient and underwent surgery.
At the time of the accident, the petitioner was employed as a Business Analyst at Genpact, Bengaluru, earning a monthly salary of Rs. 50,000.

The petitioner has stated that due to the injuries sustained, he has suffered a permanent disability,
resulting in loss of earning capacity and reduction in income.
He has also incurred expenditures of Rs. 2,00,000 towards medical treatment, conveyance, and incidental expenses.

On these grounds,
the petitioner has sought compensation from Respondent No. 1 and Respondent No. 2 for the injuries, disability, loss of income, and expenses incurred.

4. In response, the respondents have appeared through their respective counsels and filed written statements:
5. Respondent No. 1 (Owner of the offending vehicle) denies negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Denies the nature and extent of the injuries sustained, as well as the petitioner's employment, income, treatment expenses, disability, and other claims.
He states that the insurance policy was in force on the date of the accident and that the driver held a valid driving license.
He further contends that the compensation claimed is excessive and exaggerated, and seeks dismissal of the petition.
6. Respondent No. 2 (Insurance Company) denies all material averments made in the petition.
It contends that the accident did not occur due to negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.

It admits that a valid insurance policy was issued and in force on the date of the accident, but liability is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy.
7.

It further contends that the owner of the offending vehicle and the policyholder failed to comply with the mandatory provisions of Section 134(c) and Section 159 of the Motor Vehicles Act and states that the driver did not hold a valid and effective driving license and that the vehicle lacked a Naveen Kumar P.N vs Pradeep K.S on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46675821/
2 valid permit and fitness certificate at the time of the accident.

8. On the basis of the above pleadings, the following Issues were framed :-
1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that he sustained injuries when he was riding in Pulsar Bike bearing no. KA-41-ED-6565 on 05-05-2022 about 5.30 p.m near Rajavanthi Forest Office, Pavagad, Tumkur Road, Rajavanthi, Tumkur District, due to to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Swift Dezire tour BS4 bearing reg no.KA-53-C-0388?
2. What compensation petitioner is entitled?
3. What order ?
9. In order to prove the claim, the Petitioner examined himself as PW.1, doctor is examined as PW-2 and got marked the documents as per Ex.P.1 to P.16.
On behalf of the respondents, the Respondent No. 2 has examined Senior Executive as RW.1 and IO as RW.2 and Respondent No.1 is examined as RW-3 and got marked 7 documents at Ex.R1 to Ex.R7.
10. I heard the counsel on both sides and have perused the material on record.

11. By considering the available materials on record and the arguments addressed by the parties, I have answered the above Issues as under:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2: Partly in affirmative.

Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:

At that time, the offending vehicle came from behind in a rash and negligent manner and collided with the petitioner's motorcycle.
As a result of the impact, the petitioner fell and sustained grievous injuries.

Further, Dr. S.A.Somashekara, orthopedic surgeon, was examined as PW-2, and medical records were produced at Exhibits P-15 and P-16.

As per the medical records, the petitioner sustained a closed fracture of both bones of the left leg,

sentences.text: During cross-examination, a suggestion was made that PW-1 had registered a false complaint to obtain compensation, which he categorically denied.
No other material admissions favorable to the respondents were elicited.

15. Respondent No. 1 denied negligence on the part of the driver, the nature and extent of injuries,
employment, income, treatment expenses, disability, and other claims, contending that the compensation claimed is excessive and exaggerated.
16. Respondent No. 2 denied the accident was caused by negligence, though it admitted that a valid insurance policy was in force, and liability is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy.
It contended that the driver did not hold a valid driving license and the vehicle lacked a valid permit and fitness certificate at the time of the accident.
17. In an attempt to disprove the petitioner's case: Respondent No. 2 examined the official as RW-1 and the Investigating Officer (IO) as RW-2, while Respondent No. 1 examined as RW-3.
No material contrary to negligence was elicited from the IO, and his evidence remained consistent with the police records.

18. Although RW-1 and RW-3 contended that the accident occurred due to negligence on the part of the petitioner, they did not produce any cogent evidence to show that the accident occurred for any reason other than the negligent driving of the offending vehicle.

19. On evaluating the entire evidence, including the oral testimony of the petitioner and medical witness, documentary evidence, and police records, it is evident that: The accident occurred solely due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle.
The petitioner sustained grievous injuries and has proven loss of income, permanent disability, and medical expenses incurred.
The respondents have failed to produce any credible evidence to rebut the petitioner's claim or to show an alternative cause of the accident.
20. As held in various precedents, the Motor Vehicles Act is a beneficial legislation, and strict proof of negligence is not required.
The charge sheet filed by the police further corroborates the negligence of the offending vehicle driver.
Accordingly, the tribunal finds in favor of the petitioner and holds the petitioner sustained injuries in the alleged Road traffic accident due to negligence of the driver of the offending car.
Consequently, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.

21. ISSUE NO.2 :-As per the medical documents, the petitioner sustained a closed fracture of both bones of the left leg, bilateral scarred ala fracture, fracture of the S2 vertebral body, and B-L-L5 spondylolysis with grade I anterolisthesis, and L5 over S1.
Due to the impact, the petitioner suffered severe injuries.
Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to A.R. Hospital, Hindupura, where he was admitted as an inpatient and underwent surgery.

sentences.text: The petitioner examined Dr. S.A. Somashekara, an orthopedic surgeon at Bowring and Lady Curzon Hospitals, Bengaluru, who produced medical records at Exs P-15 and P-16.

Dr.
S.A.Somashekara confirmed that the petitioner sustained the above-mentioned injuries and stated that the petitioner underwent CRIF with LMIC nailing of the tibia.
He clinically and radiologically examined the petitioner for the purpose of disability assessment.
The petitioner complained of low back pain, difficulty in walking, climbing stairs, inability to squat or sit cross-legged, difficulty bending forward, and inability to lift weight.
Based on his examination, PW-1 assessed the total disability of the spine and left lower limb at 48% and 24% of the whole body, respectively.

23. During cross-examination, PW-1 admitted that he had not personally treated the petitioner, and further stated that both fractures were healed and the petitioner was capable of performing day-to-day activities with some difficulty.

It is pertinent to note that PW-1 did not provide a specific opinion regarding functional disability, which refers to the actual impact of the injuries on the petitioner's ability to perform daily activities and earn a livelihood.

24. Considering the nature and location of the injuries, particularly the involvement of the spine and tibia, which are vital for mobility and balance, the tribunal holds that the injuries sustained by the petitioner definitely affect his locomotion, mobility and ability to balance the body, thereby impacting his overall functional capacity.
Accordingly, the tribunal reasonably assesses the permanent functional disability of the petitioner at 10% of the whole body.
25. In the petition the age of the petitioner is mentioned as 35 years.

Ex.P.11 - Aadhar card of the petitioner shows that he was born on 1986, the same is considered, then age of the petitioner as on the date of accident as 36 years and the multiplier applicable to the case on hand is 15.
26.
At time of the accident, the petitioner was 36 years old and he was working as a Business Analist Genpact, Bengaluru, and was earning a monthly salary of Rs.50,000/-.
It is asserted that he has lost his earning capacity and income due to accidental injuries.
However, the petitioner has not produced any documents to substantiate his income.
In the absence of proof of income, this tribunal is of the opinion that the notional income to be assessed as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority.
Since the accident has been occurred in the year 2022, notional income Rs.15,500/- per month is taken for the assessment of compensation.

27. Thus this tribunal is of the opinion that the petitioner who sustained the injuries is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
28. Loss of future income on account of permanent disability: Considering the petitioner's grievous injury which has resulted in performing daily vocational activities, this court is of the opinion that the functional disability of 10% is reasonable and just.
29.
The petitioner was 36 years old as on date of alleged accident and the multiplier applicable to the petitioner as per decision laid down by Hon'ble Apex court in Sarla Verma's case is at 15.
The notional income taken as Rs.15,500 x 12 x 15 x 10/100= Rs.2,79,000/- towards loss of future income.

sentences.text: Pain and sufferings:

So far as the compensation under non-pecuniary damages are concerned,
considering the nature of the injury, which has resulted in difficulty in mobility and in performing daily vocational activities, as well as the duration of inpatient treatment and physical and mental suffering endured by the petitioner, this tribunal is of the opinion that an amount of .40,000/-
would be just and fair compensation under the head of pain and sufferings.
31. Loss of amenities of life: undoubtedly the petitioner is suffering from difficulties in performing day to day activities and is facing continuous hardship due to the disability.
Therefore this tribunal finds to appropriate to award a sum .30,000/- under head of loss of amenities of life.
32. Medical expenses:
Under the pecuniary damages, expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization and medicines, the Petitioner has relied on medical bills at Ex.P.9 for Rs.1,43,195/-.
On perusal of these medical bills, it reveals that the Petitioner has spent .1,43,195/- towards medical expenses.
The medical bills appears to be genuine.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for medical expenses of .1,43,195/- towards Medical Expenses.
33. Future medical expenses:
PW-2 has deposed that petitioner required one more surgery for removal of implant, which would cost around Rs.40,000/-.

Considering the petitioner's ongoing medical needs, permanent condition, and potential future surgery, this tribunal is of the opinion that it would be just and reasonable to award Rs.15,000/- towards future medical expenses.
34. Conveyance, food and nourishment charges:
Ex.P.8 -Discharge summary shows that Petitioner underwent inpatient treatment at A.R. Hospital, Hindupur from 05-05-2022 to 16-05-2022 i.e, for a period of 12 days.
Therefore, it is just and reasonable to award compensation of .12,000/- under the head of conveyance, food and nourishment charges.
35. Loss of earning during laid up period:

With regard to the loss of earnings during treatment period, Considering the nature of the injury, which has resulted in significant difficulty in mobility and in carrying out daily vocational activities, as well as the duration of impatient treatment and recovery, this tribunal considers the 3 months for rest is considered .

As the monthly income of the Petitioner is already considered as .16,000/- per month, loss of earning during laid up period would be .16,000 x 3 = Rs.48,000/-.
36.

Thus the compensation awarded under the various heads are as under:

37. Liability:

Respondent No. 2 contended that the owner of the offending vehicle violated the terms and conditions of the insurance policy because the driver did not possess a valid driving license on the date of the accident.

It was specifically alleged that the driver only held a learner's license and operated the vehicle without any instructor, and therefore, Respondent No. 2 claimed it was not liable to indemnify the owner or pay compensation to the petitioner.

38. To substantiate this contention, an official of Respondent No. 2 was examined as RW-1, who 3+deposed that the driver did not possess a valid license and drove the vehicle without an instructor, which constituted a breach of the Motor Vehicles Act and the insurance policy terms. The Investigation Officer of Crime No. 73/2022 was examined as RW-2, who stated that the owner had produced the RC and insurance policy but not the driver's license.
RW-2 also admitted during cross-examination that no instructor accompanied the driver at the time of the accident.

39. Contrary to this, the driver of the offending vehicle was examined as RW-3, who produced his learner license at Exhibit R6 and deposed that his brother was accompanying him as an instructor at the time of the accident.

He reliance upon the decision rendered in 2019 ACJ 278 Shantawwa V Ajitsingh and another and MFA no 20655/2011, Senior Divisional Manager, National Insurance Co.
Ltd V Jyotiba Appaji Shigate and others.

sentences.text:
40. While RW-3 denied earlier suggestions to the contrary, no documentary evidence, eyewitnesses,
or other material were produced by Respondent No. 2 to substantiate that no instructor was present.
41. It is undisputed that the offending vehicle was covered under a valid insurance policy on the date of the accident.
However, the insurance company failed to prove that the driver was unaccompanied by an instructor at the time of the accident.
If an instructor had truly been absent, the Investigation Officer could have recorded this fact in the charge sheet, but there is no such mention.

42. In view of the above, the tribunal finds that the contention of Respondent No. 2 holds no merit,
and the insurance company is liable to indemnify the owner and pay compensation to the petitioner.
Accordingly, Issue No. 2 is answered partly in the affirmative.

43. ISSUE NO.3 : In view of the above discussion, reasons stated and findings given to above issues,
I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Claim Petition filed under Sec.166 of M.V.Act is allowed in part with cost.

Petitioner is awarded compensation of Rs.5,67,195/- together with interest @ 6% p.a.
(except future medical expenses) from the date of petition till the date of deposit with the Tribunal.
